checks.claim: In a loaded beam bridge the top of the beam is squeezed (compression) while the bottom is stretched (tension).
checks.why: Several independent sources (ISBE bridge unit, Midas, a US patent) state compression at the top and tension at the bottom.

sources.title: Bridge Design and Construction Unit: Technology
Understanding Beam Bridges: Design, Components, and Construction Methods

checks.claim: Floods and scour are the leading cause of US bridge failures. One study of failures from 1989 to 2000 put them at about 53%, and other estimates range from roughly 48% to 60%.
checks.why: The 53% figure is 'almost 53%' and covers flood and scour combined, not scour alone. It comes from a single 1989-2000 sample inflated by the 1993 flood. Other sources give 48% and 60%, so 'more than half' is not safe.

checks.claim: Piling rocks (riprap) around a pier's foot is a standard defence against scour.
checks.why: Sources describe riprap as the most commonly used pier scour countermeasure. It must be designed and sized properly, since some reviews note its deficiencies.

checks.claim: A 100 m steel bridge span grows about 6 cm when the temperature rises by 50 degrees C (steel expands about 12 millionths per degree).
checks.why: The coefficient of about 12e-6 per °C is sourced (AASHTO 6.5e-6 per °F is about 11.7e-6 per °C). The arithmetic 12e-6 x 100 m x 50 = 0.06 m checks out.
